statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES; Tail remains modestly above the block threshold after Tuesday's technology-led decline.
recommendation: The published policy mapping remains elevated while overnight retracement quality is unresolved; Wednesday's EIA and FOMC sequences are the next major checkpoints.
headline: Technology-led downside remains elevated into overnight reopening
body: Tuesday closed with a 1.33% Nasdaq decline, a 5% semiconductor-index drop, negative breadth and the VIX at 15.84. Long yields and oil remained elevated amid unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption. After the daily futures maintenance interval, independent post-reopen NQ bar evidence is still limited, so Tail is held in the high-20s rather than escalated further.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 UTC clock hours, Tail progressed from low/mixed overnight to WATCH during the European morning, then moved into an elevated trend-down block from 09:00 UTC. It peaked at 32% in the U.S. afternoon before easing to 27% during the post-close maintenance hour.
outlookSummary: Overnight Tail is conditional on whether the Tuesday decline meaningfully retraces. Wednesday's EIA report is an oil/inflation checkpoint, while the FOMC minutes are the main scheduled Tail window because the current market is highly rates-sensitive and the interpretation can unfold in multiple stages.

forecast.analysis: Tuesday's technology-led decline and negative breadth remain the dominant evidence after the daily futures maintenance break. Independent post-reopen NQ bar evidence is still sparse, so Tail stays elevated but is not raised beyond the high-20s.

forecast.analysis: First post-maintenance hour: prior-session downside alignment remains relevant, but continuation is conditional on whether reopening pullbacks fail. Tail remains elevated while Stress stays extreme.
Overnight price discovery remains a continuation checkpoint. Tail stays just above the block threshold unless meaningful retracement and cross-asset easing become visible.
By this hour the forecast allows for stabilization if retracements develop; absent renewed extension, Tail falls to WATCH while geopolitical and rates Stress remain extreme.
Overnight liquidity is thinner and the prior selloff still matters, but without observed renewed extension the conditional Tail path eases further into WATCH.
Risk continues to decay conditionally if NQ does not retest or hold near prior-session extremes. Persistent oil and rates pressure keeps Stress elevated.
Late Asia hours are modeled as WATCH: the prior trend is still relevant, but future continuation is not assumed without fresh one-way price evidence.
Approaching Europe, Tail remains WATCH because the selloff can re-accelerate if yields, oil and technology breadth realign; otherwise retracement quality is the main invalidation.
European open is a cross-asset confirmation checkpoint. Tail remains WATCH unless equities, yields, oil and semiconductor weakness re-align into a renewed one-way move.
European price discovery remains important for whether Tuesday's U.S. technology weakness carries forward. The forecast stays WATCH and conditional.
Mid-Europe hours retain WATCH because geopolitical and long-yield Stress can transmit back into U.S. technology, but no future extension is assumed.
Late European morning is modeled slightly higher as U.S. premarket participation builds; persistent downside breadth would be required to lift Tail further.
U.S. premarket liquidity increases. Tail is WATCH as prior-session semiconductor weakness and high yields remain relevant, with no assumption that the trend resumes.
U.S. premarket participation is building. Tail remains WATCH unless prior-session downside breadth, yields and technology weakness re-align into a persistent one-way setup before the cash open.
The final pre-open hour is a conditional continuation checkpoint. Tail remains WATCH; a higher state requires observed downside efficiency rather than the prior session's weakness alone.
The 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open is the first major price-discovery checkpoint. Tail reaches the block threshold conditionally if opening-auction weakness persists through failed retracements.

The EIA petroleum report at 14:30 UTC overlaps early cash-session price discovery. Tail stays elevated conditionally because oil-to-yields transmission could reinforce technology weakness; no release outcome is assumed.
Post-EIA and post-open digestion is modeled at WATCH if meaningful retracements and cross-asset easing emerge. Renewed one-way extension would invalidate that conditional decay.
Pre-FOMC conditions remain WATCH. Event importance raises Stress, while Tail stays below block absent already-observed one-way structure into the release.
FOMC minutes are the primary scheduled policy checkpoint. Conditional Tail is elevated because the current market is rates-sensitive; direction and any second leg remain unobserved until the release.
The first post-minutes hour carries elevated conditional Tail for bond-yield interpretation and possible delayed equity repricing; the forecast does not assume that continuation will occur.
A delayed second-leg window remains possible after the minutes if yields and technology weakness align. Tail stays elevated while cross-asset stabilization remains the key conditional invalidation.
Late-session risk is modeled back to WATCH if post-minutes price discovery is orderly and retracements occur; renewed extension would invalidate that decay path.
Final forecast hour remains WATCH because FOMC interpretation can persist into the close, but the model requires observed directional efficiency before re-escalating Tail.

WATCH reflects conditional stabilization if overnight retracements develop while geopolitical and rates Stress stays extreme.
